Import failures, hidden dependencies, unsupported behavior, or failed audio verification must be reported as capability gaps rather than treated as authorization for a procedural substitute.","title":"Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint","summary":"A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens. A decorative obstacle scene or a timer alone is insufficient.","answerId":null}],"clarifications":[],"playerExperience":{"title":"Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Sprint","summary":"A compact solo sky-parkour run contained under the supplied namespace. The course begins on a safe floating spawn island with a bright Start pad, a visible chain of floating steps, three numbered checkpoint beacons, a moving-platform crossing, a high-contrast fall zone below, and a finish arch visible in the distance. In the first minute, the player sees the route and HUD immediately, steps onto Start to begin the timer, learns the comfortable jump spacing, reaches Checkpoint 1, and receives a beacon activation animation plus synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The route then leads through the moving-platform crossing to Checkpoint 2, an ascending final step sequence to Checkpoint 3, and the finish.

Progress is server-authoritative and ordered: only the next checkpoint activates, while touching later checkpoints early has no effect. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the last valid checkpoint without resetting checkpoint progress or elapsed time. The finish only accepts a player who has activated all three checkpoints. Completion freezes the result time and presents a deliberate Replay button; replay resets the run, progress, timer, character position, checkpoint visuals, and moving-course state where required.

Assumptions chosen from the user's permission to choose reasonable style and layout: the timer starts on physical contact with the Start pad; checkpoint order is Start → 1 → 2 → 3 → Finish; horizontal jumps generally remain around 4–6 studs with broad landing surfaces; the moving platform uses a short, readable route with safe boarding areas; replay is never automatic. The experience has no persistence, purchases, competitive systems, or multiplayer-facing features. Internally, player state is still indexed and cleaned per UserId so respawn and server lifecycle behavior remain safe.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and complete obby/course components must be searched and inspected before implementation decisions. Useful verified geometry, scripts, motion, animation, and media will be retained. Main traversable surfaces use pale cloud-white and cool cyan materials; structural undersides use deeper blue-violet tones to give each island a designed silhouette. Checkpoints are tall numbered beacon assemblies with dormant cyan rings and a vivid green-white activated state. The finish is a larger gold-white arch that remains visually distinct from checkpoints.

Compose the course as one shallow rising arc rather than a sprawling straight line. From spawn, the player should see Checkpoint 1 in the near foreground, the moving-platform crossing and Checkpoint 2 at mid-distance, then Checkpoint 3 and the finish as elevated focal points. Keep landing surfaces broad, edge profiles crisp, and decorative elements away from jump paths.

The fall hazard is unmistakable: a broad red-magenta warning volume or plane sits below the course, with luminous warning strips and downward chevrons at exposed transition edges. It must contrast strongly with the cool safe-route palette and remain legible without relying on text alone.

Checkpoint activation should be observable from the player camera: illuminate or recolor the beacon, expand or pulse a ring, and briefly emphasize the checkpoint number. Preserve an imported component's verified animation if it provides equivalent feedback. The confirmation sound begins in the same activation phase as the visible response. Later checkpoints remain visibly dormant until their turn.

The HUD is compact and readable on desktop and touch: a top-center checkpoint label such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3,” a large tabular elapsed time beneath it, and restrained status messaging. On completion, show a centered result card with the final time and a generously sized Replay button suitable for touch. Use strong contrast, safe-area-aware margins, rounded panels, and text sizing that remains readable on narrow phone screens.
